title: Verified model evidence pack + sales flows
body:
Document purpose:

This is a compact, seller-friendly "evidence pack" and playbook for the "Verified Profiles" feature in the model catalog. It pairs crisp positioning with an evidence matrix and conversation flows for AE/SEs to use during discovery and technical demos. The aim is to reduce friction in selection conversations, shorten evaluation cycles, and convert trials into Dedicated/Private conversations by surfacing repeatable quality signals.

Audience:
- Sales (Account Execs, Solutions Engineers)
- GTM content & enablement
- Product marketing for model catalog pages

Core positioning (one-liners):
- Engineering-first quality: "Verified Profiles" surface the reproducible test signals that matter — latency, 99th percentile tail, regression-stable evaluation sets — so teams can choose models with predictable economics and behavior.
- Business-safe adoption: Verified Profiles combine open-model transparency with Redwood's serving benchmarks and rollout controls, letting buyers adopt open models while meeting SLAs and security needs.

Elevator pitches (short):
- For engineering leads: "Pick models based on repeatable evidence, not hype — our Verified Profiles show you how a model performs for requests like yours and what tradeoffs you get for latency, cost, and accuracy."
- For procurement/infosec: "Verified Profiles reduce procurement risk by attaching reproducible benchmarking and provenance metadata to open models, and defining migration paths to Dedicated/Private with minimal rework."

Top 6 proof points to highlight (one-sentence each):
1) Benchmarked performance: standardized Redwood microbench suite including p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput under realistic batch profiles.
2) Regression guardrails: weekly eval runs against pinned prompt sets with automated alerts for quality drift.
3) Cost guidance: empirically derived tokens/us and suggested quantization/seq-length knobs for expected unit-cost savings.
4) Compatibility matrix: runtime/quantization compatibility and fallback variants to preserve uptime.
5) Security & provenance: model source, license, and hash + KMS-ready keying patterns for Private deployments.
6) Customer case snippet: short anecdote showing 30% token-cost reduction after switching to a Verified Profile + batching config.

Evidence matrix (seller cheat-sheet) — quick visual you can read aloud:
- Matrix columns: Signal | What we measure | Thresholds | Why it matters | Sales script line
- Example rows (pasteable):
  * Latency (p95) | 120ms @ 8 concurrency (g4dn-like) | <200ms = preferred | Predicts UI responsiveness; affects user retention | "This profile hits p95 <200ms under your concurrency range — you won't get janky UI responses when load spikes."
  * Token cost (tokens/sec-equivalent) | tokens/sec + batch efficiency | 15–30% cheaper than baseline = good | Direct impact on TCO and unit economics | "We estimate a 20% savings on tokens for chat workloads with our suggested config."
  * Semantic accuracy (eval set F1 / human QA) | task-specific evals (support routing, summarization) | baseline ±3% | Ensures output quality won't break flows | "This model stays within our quality guardrails for support summarization prompts."
  * Regression stability | weekly eval CI failures | 0 unexpected regressions in last 30d | Reduces surprise breakages in prod | "We run continuous checks and can show you the weekly history for the profile."

Competitive contrasts — quick bullets to use in objection handling:
- Versus general LLM API providers: Redwood ties open-model transparency to serving economics and rollout controls (not just model access). Focus: predictable production behavior.
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: Self-hosting gives control but requires heavy bench and rollout investments; Verified Profiles compress that work into a consumable artifact. Focus: time-to-safe-production.
- Versus model-marketplaces: Marketplaces list models; Verified Profiles curate and quantify tradeoffs for the same open models so buyers can make operational decisions, not just pick a name.

Common buyer questions and suggested responses:
- Q: "How do you generate these profiles?"
  A: "Standardized bench harness + task-specific evals + runtime traces. We publish seed prompts, hardware baseline, and the exact runtime config used so teams can reproduce or test themselves."
- Q: "Can I trust open-source model weights?"
  A: "Profiles include provenance (source URL, license, hash) and a compatibility note for our Private deployment. For regulated workloads we recommend Private with KMS and a short audit checklist we can share."
- Q: "How often are profiles updated?"
  A: "Profiles are updated on model releases and weekly regression runs; clients on Dedicated can opt into private cadence and finer-grain pinning."

Sales flows (playbook snippets):
- Discovery call (10–15m): 1) Confirm workload type (chat, summarization, rerank). 2) Ask SLOs (p95 latency, throughput, cost target, quality guardrails). 3) Surface the closest Verified Profiles and read 2–3 evidence bullets. 4) Propose a short eval: 7–14 day trial with Redwood-hosted profile and a templated prompt set.
- Technical deep-dive (30–60m, SE-led): 1) Walk the evidence matrix for the selected profiles. 2) Share traces, KV cache behavior, and expected billing delta. 3) If security-sensitive, demo Private deployment options and audit artifacts. 4) Agree success criteria and rollback/fallback plan.

Objection-safe language (for AEs):
- "If latency or behavior is critical, we can run a short reproducible bench in your environment or provide our results with the exact harness to validate."
- "We don't claim 'best' — we claim 'predictable' and 'reproducible' tradeoffs. Verified Profiles are about lowering rollout risk."

Field playbook attachments to create (author/owner recommendations):
- Short reproducible bench harness for SEs (owner: Eng Applied ML) — link pinned in CRM.
- One-pager with 3 customer examples (owner: PM Product Marketing).
- Slide deck for AEs with objection handling and a 2-slide evidence snapshot per profile.

Metrics to track to validate impact (recommended KPIs):
- Time from first demo to evaluation kick-off (target <7d).
- Trial -> paid conversion rate for accounts that used a Verified Profile (target +15% vs baseline).
- Number of security-close cases converted to Private after profile review.
- SE time saved per deal (qualitative feedback).

Next steps / open questions (for roadmap sync):
1) Define the canonical customer prompt templates per workload — who owns? (PM + SE)
2) Finalize evidence publication UX in catalog page (product + eng) — publish date: end of Q1.
3) Create a lightweight audit checklist for infosec reviewers (security)
4) SE enablement session planned (date suggestion: 2025-02-12)

Appendix: sample AE lines (copy-paste)
- "For your use case, the 'Verified Profile — chat-medium' shows a stable p95 under 180ms and a 19% cost advantage when you apply our batching recommendations. We can run the same harness against a subset of your traffic in 48 hours."
- "If you need deterministic behavior, we can lock a profile to a model hash and run weekly regressions as part of the contract."

Notes & provenance:
- This doc synthesizes insights from the model-evals backlog, customer pilots (pilot id: RED-PILOT-58), and SE feedback channels (#se-deals). See linked artifacts for reproducibility references.
- Drafted by Aisha Patel — feedback requested from product marketing and Eng Applied ML before publishing to the catalog.
